_meta.indication: EGATEN is indicated for the treatment of fascioliasis in patients 6 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.nct: No NCT number; registered as ISRCTN 75869075
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), open-label, single center trial in Vietnam comparing Egaten 10 mg/kg x 2 (12 hours apart) vs. artesunate 4 mg/kg once a day for 10 days in acute fascioliasis.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients meeting the case definition for fascioliasis, over 8 years of age, hospitalized with acute disease.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: resolution of abdominal pain at hospital discharge (day 10).
pivotal_trials.result: On the primary endpoint (no abdominal pain at discharge), TCBZ was numerically inferior to the comparator artesunate: 44/50 (88%) vs. 50/50 (100%), diff -12% (95% CI -21.5, -1.5; p=0.027), i.e., TCBZ did not beat artesunate on the primary endpoint. At 3 months post-treatment (a secondary outcome), 92% (46/50) and 76% (38/50) of patients in the TCBZ and artesunate arms respectively had no clinical symptoms (risk difference 16%; 95% CI 1.7%, 30.8%; p=0.035), favoring TCBZ.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) at the 20 mg/kg dose are abdominal pain, hyperhidrosis, nausea, decreased appetite, headache, urticaria, diarrhea, vomiting, musculoskeletal chest pain, and pruritus. Abdominal pain was very common (56% at 10 mg/kg; 93% at 20 mg/kg). Triclabendazole may prolong the QT interval.
target_moa: Triclabendazole is an anthelmintic (benzimidazole derivative); its mechanism against Fasciola is not fully understood but the drug and its active metabolites penetrate the fluke tegument, altering the resting tegumental membrane potential, interfering with microtubule structure and function, and inhibiting protein and enzyme synthesis, resulting in death of the fluke.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.
